quests.hint: This is the list of food and drink options available at a restaurant.
quests.explanation: 'The menu' uses 'the' (it's a specific document). 'Look at the menu,' 'read the menu,' and 'ask for the menu' are the most natural English expressions.
quests.textToSpeak: The waiter brought us the ___ and recommended the fish of the day.
quests.correctAnswer: The waiter brought us the menu and recommended the fish of the day.

quests.hint: This is the verb that means to tell a waiter what food or drink you want.
quests.explanation: 'Order' is both a verb ('I'd like to order') and a noun ('take your order'). 'Place an order' is a slightly more formal version used in business settings.
quests.textToSpeak: Are you ready to ___, or do you need a few more minutes to decide?
quests.correctAnswer: Are you ready to order, or do you need a few more minutes to decide?

quests.hint: This is the sweet course served at the end of a meal - the final part of dinner.
quests.explanation: 'Dessert' (two s's) is the sweet course. Don't confuse it with 'desert' (one s) - the sandy landscape. 'For dessert' is the correct English preposition.
quests.textToSpeak: After the main course, we shared a chocolate cake for ___.
quests.correctAnswer: After the main course, we shared a chocolate cake for dessert.

quests.hint: This is the document or card that allows you to travel on a bus, train, or plane.
quests.explanation: 'Buy a ticket,' 'book a ticket,' and 'show your ticket' are the key collocations. 'Return ticket' means round trip; 'single ticket' means one-way.
quests.textToSpeak: You need to buy a ___ before you can board the train to London.
quests.correctAnswer: You need to buy a ticket before you can board the train to London.

quests.hint: This is the official document with your photo that proves your identity abroad.
quests.explanation: 'Passport' is always countable. 'Show your passport,' 'renew your passport,' and 'passport control' are key travel collocations in English.
quests.textToSpeak: Do not forget to bring your ___ when travelling to another country.
quests.correctAnswer: Do not forget to bring your passport when travelling to another country.

quests.hint: This is the general word for all the bags and suitcases you travel with.
quests.explanation: 'Luggage' is uncountable: 'hand luggage,' 'carry luggage,' 'check in luggage.' Never 'a luggage.' 'Luggage allowance' is how much you're permitted to bring.
quests.textToSpeak: The airline allows each passenger to bring one piece of hand ___.
quests.correctAnswer: The airline allows each passenger to bring one piece of hand luggage.

quests.hint: This is a prediction of what the weather will be like in the coming days.
quests.explanation: 'Weather forecast' is the full compound noun. 'According to the forecast' and 'check the forecast' are natural phrases. Forecasts are often checked on a phone app.
quests.textToSpeak: According to the weather ___, it will be warm and dry all week long.
quests.correctAnswer: According to the weather forecast, it will be warm and dry all week long.

quests.hint: This is the measurement of how hot or cold the air or a substance is.
quests.explanation: 'Temperature' is measured in degrees. 'The temperature dropped' (went colder) or 'rose' (got warmer). 'Take someone's temperature' means to measure their body heat.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ dropped below zero overnight and there was frost on all the cars.
quests.correctAnswer: The temperature dropped below zero overnight and there was frost on all the cars.

quests.hint: This is a long waterproof coat worn to protect you from rain when it is wet outside.
quests.explanation: 'Raincoat' is one word. 'Wear a raincoat,' 'put on your raincoat,' and 'pack a raincoat' are natural collocations. 'Mac' or 'mackintosh' is a British synonym.
quests.textToSpeak: She wore her ___ and wellies because the weather outside was terrible.
quests.correctAnswer: She wore her raincoat and wellies because the weather outside was terrible.

quests.hint: This is physical activity done to improve health, strength, or fitness.
quests.explanation: 'Exercise' is both uncountable ('do exercise,' 'take exercise') and countable ('an exercise'). 'Regular exercise' and 'take exercise' are the most natural phrases.
quests.textToSpeak: Regular ___ is one of the best things you can do for your long-term health.
quests.correctAnswer: Regular exercise is one of the best things you can do for your long-term health.

quests.hint: This is the activity of moving through water using your arms and legs for fitness.
quests.explanation: 'Go swimming' uses 'go + verb-ing.' 'Swimming pool' is where you do it. 'Swimming costume' or 'swimsuit' is what you wear. 'Swim' is the irregular verb form.
quests.textToSpeak: She goes ___ three times a week to stay fit and reduce her stress levels.
quests.correctAnswer: She goes swimming three times a week to stay fit and reduce her stress levels.

quests.hint: This is a place with equipment for physical exercise, such as treadmills and weights.
quests.explanation: 'Join the gym' and 'go to the gym' are the key collocations. 'Gym membership' is what you pay for. 'Hit the gym' is an informal phrase meaning to go and exercise.
quests.textToSpeak: He joined the local ___ and started training five days a week.
quests.correctAnswer: He joined the local gym and started training five days a week.

quests.hint: This is the set of instructions telling you how to prepare and cook a specific dish.
quests.explanation: 'Follow a recipe,' 'try a new recipe,' and 'look up a recipe' are the most natural collocations. 'Recipe book' or 'cookbook' is where recipes are collected.
quests.textToSpeak: She followed a simple online ___ to make the most amazing chocolate cake.
quests.correctAnswer: She followed a simple online recipe to make the most amazing chocolate cake.

quests.hint: These are the individual food items needed to make a particular dish or recipe.
quests.explanation: 'Ingredients' is usually plural. 'Fresh ingredients,' 'the right ingredients,' and 'list of ingredients' are common. 'The secret ingredient' is used idiomatically too.
quests.textToSpeak: Before you start cooking, make sure you have all the ___ ready to go.
quests.correctAnswer: Before you start cooking, make sure you have all the ingredients ready to go.

quests.hint: This is the cooking appliance that heats food by surrounding it with hot air.
quests.explanation: 'Preheat the oven,' 'put something in the oven,' and 'take something out of the oven' are the key patterns. 'Oven-ready' means prepared for direct cooking.
quests.textToSpeak: Preheat the ___ to 180 degrees before putting in the biscuits.
quests.correctAnswer: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees before putting in the biscuits.

quests.hint: This is a specific time you have arranged to meet someone, often a professional.
quests.explanation: 'Make an appointment,' 'book an appointment,' and 'miss an appointment' are key collocations. 'Doctor's appointment' and 'dental appointment' are very common.
quests.textToSpeak: I need to make a dental ___ for a routine check-up as soon as possible.
quests.correctAnswer: I need to make a dental appointment for a routine check-up as soon as possible.

quests.hint: This is the final date or time by which a task or piece of work must be completed.
quests.explanation: 'Meet a deadline' (succeed) or 'miss a deadline' (fail). 'Tight deadline' means very little time. 'Work to a deadline' means to work toward a time limit.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ for submitting the report is Friday at five o'clock sharp.
quests.correctAnswer: The deadline for submitting the report is Friday at five o'clock sharp.

quests.hint: This is a plan that lists times and activities arranged in order for a period.
quests.explanation: 'Check your schedule,' 'look at your schedule,' and 'fit something into your schedule' are the key collocations. 'Busy schedule' and 'tight schedule' are common.
quests.textToSpeak: Please check your ___ and let me know when you are available to meet.
quests.correctAnswer: Please check your schedule and let me know when you are available to meet.

quests.hint: This is the annual celebration of the day a person was born.
quests.explanation: 'Happy birthday!' is the standard greeting. 'Birthday party,' 'birthday cake,' and 'birthday card' are common compounds. 'On your birthday' is the correct preposition.
quests.textToSpeak: She baked a special cake for her son's ___ party on Saturday afternoon.
quests.correctAnswer: She baked a special cake for her son's birthday party on Saturday afternoon.

quests.hint: This is a gift given to someone to show care or mark a special occasion.
quests.explanation: 'Present' and 'gift' are almost interchangeable. 'Give someone a present,' 'open a present,' and 'wrap a present' are key collocations. 'A birthday present' is very common.
quests.textToSpeak: He bought her a beautiful necklace as a ___ for their anniversary.
quests.correctAnswer: He bought her a beautiful necklace as a present for their anniversary.

quests.hint: This verb means to do something enjoyable to mark a special event or achievement.
quests.explanation: 'Celebrate' takes the pattern 'celebrate + noun': 'celebrate a birthday,' 'celebrate a victory.' 'Celebrations' (noun) and 'celebratory dinner' are related forms.
quests.textToSpeak: The whole team went out to dinner to ___ completing the difficult project.
quests.correctAnswer: The whole team went out to dinner to celebrate completing the difficult project.

quests.hint: This is the amount of money asked for a product or service.
quests.explanation: 'Price' is a noun: 'the price of,' 'at a price,' 'price tag.' 'What's the price?' and 'the price is' are natural. 'Pricey' is an informal adjective meaning expensive.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ of the jacket was far too high, so she decided not to buy it.
quests.correctAnswer: The price of the jacket was far too high, so she decided not to buy it.

quests.hint: This is the printed paper proof of a purchase showing what you bought and how much you paid.
quests.explanation: 'Keep your receipt,' 'ask for a receipt,' and 'show your receipt' are the key collocations. Without a receipt, shops may refuse to exchange or refund goods.
quests.textToSpeak: Always keep your ___ in case you need to return or exchange the item.
quests.correctAnswer: Always keep your receipt in case you need to return or exchange the item.

quests.hint: This is the money returned to you when you return a product or cancel a service.
quests.explanation: 'Get a refund,' 'issue a refund,' and 'ask for a refund' are the key collocations. 'Full refund' means all your money back. 'Refund policy' is important to check.
quests.textToSpeak: The shop gave her a full ___ because the item was faulty when it arrived.
quests.correctAnswer: The shop gave her a full refund because the item was faulty when it arrived.

quests.hint: This is a pain in your head - one of the most common everyday complaints.
quests.explanation: 'Have a headache' is the correct English structure, not 'feel headache.' 'Terrible headache,' 'splitting headache,' and 'bad headache' are common intensifiers.
quests.textToSpeak: She had a terrible ___ and had to lie down in a quiet, darkened room.
quests.correctAnswer: She had a terrible headache and had to lie down in a quiet, darkened room.

quests.hint: This is any substance used to treat an illness or relieve symptoms of pain.
quests.explanation: 'Take medicine' (not 'drink medicine' in English). 'Prescribed medicine' requires a doctor's prescription. 'Over-the-counter medicine' can be bought without a prescription.
quests.textToSpeak: The doctor prescribed some ___ and told her to get plenty of rest.
quests.correctAnswer: The doctor prescribed some medicine and told her to get plenty of rest.

quests.hint: This is the British English word for a pharmacy - also used to mean the shop itself.
quests.explanation: 'Chemist's' (with apostrophe-s) is the everyday British English term for a pharmacy. 'Go to the chemist's' is more commonly used in spoken British English than 'pharmacy.'
quests.textToSpeak: You can buy that particular cream without a prescription from any local ___.
quests.correctAnswer: You can buy that particular cream without a prescription from any local chemist's.

quests.hint: This is the information given to help someone find their way to a destination.
quests.explanation: 'Give directions,' 'ask for directions,' and 'follow directions' are the key collocations. 'Take a wrong turn' means to go the wrong way when following directions.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you give me ___ to the nearest underground station from here?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you give me directions to the nearest underground station from here?

quests.hint: This is a point where you change direction - left or right - on a route.
quests.explanation: 'Take the first turning on the left' means turn left at the first junction. 'Turning' (British English) is also called a 'turn' in American English.
quests.textToSpeak: Take the second ___ on the left and the hotel is on your right.
quests.correctAnswer: Take the second turning on the left and the hotel is on your right.

quests.hint: This is a circular junction where roads meet and traffic flows in one direction.
quests.explanation: 'Go around the roundabout' and 'take the third exit at the roundabout' are standard navigation instructions in British English. Common in the UK.
quests.textToSpeak: Go straight through the ___ and then follow the signs for the town centre.
quests.correctAnswer: Go straight through the roundabout and then follow the signs for the town centre.
